questions.q: Acidic chyme enters the duodenum. Which hormone most directly stimulates pancreatic duct cells to secrete bicarbonate-rich fluid?
questions.explain: Acid in the duodenum stimulates S cells to release secretin. Secretin acts mainly on pancreatic ductal cells to increase bicarbonate-rich fluid secretion, helping neutralise gastric acid.

questions.q: A fatty meal reaches the duodenum. Which hormone causes gallbladder contraction and promotes enzyme-rich pancreatic secretion?
questions.explain: Fatty acids and amino acids in the duodenum stimulate I cells to release cholecystokinin (CCK). CCK contracts the gallbladder and stimulates pancreatic acinar enzyme secretion; secretin primarily promotes bicarbonate-rich ductal secretion.

questions.q: During storage of bile between meals, which process increases its concentration within the gallbladder?
options: Absorption of water and electrolytes across the gallbladder mucosa
Active secretion of large amounts of bicarbonate into the bile
Conversion of bile salts into pancreatic enzymes
Continuous addition of water by the gallbladder epithelium
questions.explain: The gallbladder concentrates stored bile by absorbing water and electrolytes through its mucosa. The bile salts, bile pigments, cholesterol and phospholipids therefore become more concentrated before bile is released into the duodenum.

open.q: How does the gallbladder concentrate bile during storage?
accept: Absorption of water and electrolytes from bile

questions.q: A patient with terminal ileal disease develops impaired enterohepatic circulation of bile salts. Which consequence is most likely?
options: Reduced bile salt pool and impaired micelle formation
Increased recycling of bile salts to the liver
Increased conversion of bilirubin to urobilinogen in the ileum
questions.explain: Bile salts are actively reabsorbed mainly in the terminal ileum and returned to the liver through portal blood. Ileal disease reduces the bile salt pool, impairing micelle formation and absorption of dietary lipids and fat-soluble vitamins.

open.q: Where are bile salts actively reabsorbed for enterohepatic circulation?

questions.q: A patient has markedly reduced activation of pancreatic proteolytic zymogens in the duodenum despite normal pancreatic secretion. Which brush-border enzyme is most likely deficient?
questions.explain: Enteropeptidase on the duodenal brush border converts trypsinogen to trypsin. Trypsin then activates other pancreatic zymogens, including chymotrypsinogen and procarboxypeptidases.

questions.q: A patient with pancreatic exocrine insufficiency has steatorrhoea. Which enzyme normally accounts for most enzymatic hydrolysis of dietary triacylglycerol in the small intestine?
questions.explain: Pancreatic lipase, assisted by colipase, hydrolyses dietary triacylglycerols mainly to 2-monoacylglycerol and free fatty acids. Deficiency impairs fat digestion and can cause steatorrhoea.

questions.q: A patient with obstructive jaundice has reduced delivery of bile salts into the intestinal lumen. Which step in lipid digestion and absorption is most directly impaired?
options: Formation of mixed micelles that carry lipid digestion products to the enterocyte surface
Hydrolysis of peptide bonds by brush-border peptidases
Conversion of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate in enterocytes
Active uptake of amino acids by sodium-coupled transporters
questions.explain: Bile salts emulsify dietary fat and form mixed micelles with products of lipid digestion. Micelles facilitate delivery of fatty acids, monoacylglycerols, cholesterol and fat-soluble vitamins to the intestinal brush border.

questions.q: A patient with dry mouth has difficulty initiating starch digestion. Which enzyme normally begins the hydrolysis of dietary starch in the oral cavity?
questions.explain: Salivary alpha-amylase begins starch digestion by hydrolysing internal alpha-1,4 glycosidic bonds, producing smaller oligosaccharides and maltose. Its activity is limited when gastric acidity inactivates it.

questions.q: A patient with chronic liver disease has reduced synthesis of bile acids. Which precursor is used by hepatocytes to produce the primary bile acids?
questions.explain: Hepatocytes synthesise the primary bile acids, cholic acid and chenodeoxycholic acid, from cholesterol. Bile acids are conjugated with glycine or taurine before secretion into bile.
